D-Trye: If he wasn't such a decent person you could almost call D-Trye machiavellian in the way he goes about it. In his own way I suppose he is. But he means well, though. Indeed, half the time he's quite mystifying. Like several in the Kingdom however, you don't often see him during the day.
Dacoda: Mate, pull your pants up, wash that crap out of your hair, stand up straight and if you shake someone's hand don't just present a limp, dead jellyfish grip. Get a job doing something you truly love and once in a while donate some money to a cause that helps those who are worse off than you. Finally, ensure you look people in the face who are talking to you and then, my boy, you will begin to change the world.
Dade: Like a piece of elastic that has gone slack and old, in an attempt to get on with his life Dade dawdles around here and there. Does he ever run? We doubt it. Time - he has oodles of it. The hustle and bustle of city-life, for instance, doesn't really get through to him and he takes ages to do the dishes. But, he's a well-meaning lad and we enjoy his company.
Daden: Daden is a paper-pusher, or at least the modern equivalent. Not really an alpha male, Daden pays his taxes and trudges to work in the uniform of the modern slave, wondering where and how things might have been different.
Daf: See Dafydd, except that this one seems to make more sense.
Dafydd: Dafydd has been compelled to turn into a complete weirdo – his Welsh heritage probably helps. He is never glum and no one knows if he has ever had a job, aside from professional skateboard rider for a while, and we only assume that because he rides one everywhere, trailing a mop of crazy hair, or what he has left of it, and possibly a line of giggling children.
Dahrol: He's a frustrating student. Not because he doesn't listen and not because he is disruptive in class, but it just takes so bloody long for anything to get inside and stick in that muddled head of his. Once the info is there, no worries. It just takes ages, that's all. I've no idea what he's doing these days, but I'll pay you $5 million if he's in England right now flying Typhoons for the RAF. No way.
Dain: Dain is going along quite nicely, but what the creative team wants to see is Dain walk to the top of the nearest mountain, hill or cliff, put his arms up in the air and scream at the heavens as loudly and for as long as he can without passing out. They think it'll do him the world of good.
Daine: Yes, he's a man and, yes, he's a wedding planner.
Dakota: A reference to two American states? Really? Are your folks the full bob, Dakota? Anyway, he keeps his head low and tries to stay out of mischief, which can’t be said for most of his male friends who, by and large, are buffoons. The end.
Dale: A small mountain lake. Calm on the surface and freezing cold, he is so deep and inviting that no one actually knows how deep he really is.
Dallan: Unfortunately Dallan didn't hear about eating vegetables until he left home. I wonder if his parents ever went to jail for abuse…anyway, considering he had a late start he's doing quite well, now. He wants to learn and he absorbs new information like a sponge. Better than that, he seems to be able to apply what he's learned. On its own this is a rare gift.
Dallas: The singer Sade sang a song about him: “Smooth operator, smooth…..operator.” (In life he is a highly functioning drug addict.)
Dalton: Dalton, how the fuck did you get yourself into this pickle? Look at  you, for god's sake. You've conned your way into this back room poker game after borrowing $15,000 off your mum (who you already owe 18 grand to), you've just gone into debt with these guys here tonight to the tune of another 5 and you're bluffing on a pair off 2's. Dalton, these blokes haven't got a sense of humour, mate. And they've got weapons. (sigh)....what are we going to do with you? Perhaps we’ll catch up with you in the next life, eh?…
Damian:
Option A:  Damian is extremely single-minded. If he is a rational man then he is capable of great things but if he isn’t, and 65% of them aren’t, then he might be so blinkered that he is potentially dangerous. The only great one is a vascular surgeon who wears a chic black leather jacket, so technically they’re not all bad – even though it was a typically ‘Damian’s’ intelligence and drive that got him there in the first place. 

Option B:  A totally anal and obnoxious cop on a power trip.
Damien: Let's hope he's not a cop, but if he can steer clear of a controlling nature Damien has the capacity to be a wonderful man. Yep, sure, he might sport a temper from time to time but it's all a product of having too much energy. If you possess a Damien, can we suggest you point him in the direction of a hobby or passtime that he loves. That'll fix him up, no worries.
Damir: Picture, if you will, the mood of the crew when Elizabeth Taylor walks onto a movie set in the 1960’s. Everyone feels better, everyone feels inspired to do their best, and even the director understands that he doesn’t have to do that much. No, Damir isn’t Elizabeth Taylor, but there is some kind of calm, regal poltergeist in his DNA.
Damo: Nothing like his painful brothers, Damo is a sensitive, funny and kind-hearted bloke who lives the physical male life; pearl farming, mining, tuna fishing, etc etc. Well-suited to the Australian summer, they are nearly always blonde.
Damon: A perfectly-weighted name for a well-weighted man, and whose core stability precludes almost all irrationality. In short, Damon is rock solid, intelligent, different and funny, and absolutely nothing gets passed him.
Dan: The all-round Mr Nice Guy that mothers and grandmothers pinch on the cheek and say, “Oooh, you’re such a beautiful boy!” He now coaches a boys’ basketball team and wears a cap everywhere he goes.
Dane: Blessed with a calm head and an imposing persona, Dane times everything to perfection.
Dani: Dani is far more sensitive and calm than Danny. Why that is no one knows. His responses take a little longer because he thinks about what he's going to say. In fact, sometimes he's quite intense, but he means well. Believe it or not he'd make a good statistician - he doesn't always have to be a tradesman.
Daniel: A clever and gentle-natured man at his core, Daniel may not be the last person you’d want next to you in a life-and-death situation and the last I heard he was answering telephones in the customer service department for most of the major banks. But, and it's a rather important 'but', Daniel does carry a morbid edge sometimes – a secret garden, if you will, that provides him with a steely gaze if things get really hairy.
Danko: Yes, Danko has friends and a social life, but he is one secretive dude. What's going on behind all those doors, brother? Something good we hope?...
Danniel:
The unexploded bomb unit arrives on the scene and they're nervous. The chief disarmer is all kitted out (the last one was killed only last week), not that it will matter if the device goes off. He bends down carefully, puts his stethascope to the metal skin of the bomb and he listens...
He's sweating, as are his team listening on the radio.
Then he smiles.
"It's okay boys," he says into the microphone. "It's a Danniel, not a Daniel."
The relief is palpable. And with that, he hits the device hard with his little hammer and the 'bomb' bursts open, covering him in harmless confetti.
Danniel.
Danny:
Danny has more energy to burn than 98% of the population and as a sensitive young man he is prone, more than most, to those early influences which can mould a personality. Like a few other members of the Kingdom, Danny has two very different outcomes. 
If he did well early, then he has channelled all this energy, both mental and physical, into a loving and productive life and he’s a funny, generous guy all round. One of the very best, actually.
If he didn’t do well early, or he was brought up on the wrong side of the tracks, then in all likelihood you’re dealing with a Danny who will feed an inferiority complex by drinking or drugging too much in an effort to expel all his anger, and he therefore makes a good boxer or bar room brawler. It’s a pity this second Danny left school early. Indeed, some martial arts guidance might completely heal him. 
No matter which Danny you are dealing with, however, keep in mind that all members of the Danny genus need to be kept busy. It’s just how they are.
Dara: The Tactician. Sure, give him shit about his name if you like but he's heard it all before. While you're giving him shit, he's scanning you like a barcode reader figuring out who you are, what you're about, where you're headed and what your true motives are. It rarely takes him long, and then he goes about his business under the cover of anonymity, rarely not succeeding because he's smarter than 88% of the population. You with me?
Darby: A girl’s name for a man in the city. Darby, how’s life? Are you parents a bit dippy? Once in a while you seem to act like a macho idiot, which is a possible reaction to your name, so we suggest letting go of all that crap and learning to exhibit your love for the world. We know you’ve got a good heart deep down. Time to bring it, cap’n. Management.
Darcy: Corrin is the champion in the bathroom department, no question, but Darcy does alright. Other than that, he’s a good guy with plenty of friends, and who expects to do quite well.
Daren:
As Jon is to John, Jacen is to Jason and Bryan is to Brian, here we have Daren. Yes, Darren and Daren sound identical but that’s where the similarities end. Daren doesn’t work with his hands, he has a much greater chance of being gay, he’s almost certainly attended some higher education institution, he is definitely more emotionally mature and he might even be an artist. In fact, if you want to break it down real quick, and this isn’t always going to be 100% by the way….
Daren = City
Darren = Country. 
Good luck!
Darian: He may or may not be gay, but he is a neat and rather refined man, irrespective. Highly intelligent, he knows most of the people whose photos grace the social pages and has probably slept with half of them.
Darien: If Darien was ever to represent his country at the olympics his chosen event would take place inside the equestrian arena. He loves all that shiny leather and the tight white riding trousers.
Dario: Here’s a message from Dario: Don’t fuckwith my friends, don’t fuckwith my family, but outside those walls I am one of the most loyal, giving, generous and ridiculously fun people you will ever meet. Amen.
Darius: Darius is one of those men who, at some point in their life, aspires to produce his magnum opus and be lauded, therein.
Darko: Darko, here's a tip from the boys in the commentary box: You don't need to tell all your friends the ins and outs of every girl you kiss or sleep with, okay hoss?
Darrell: Darrell was never on NASA’s payroll but who cares? He knows First Aid, he understands when someone is under stress and as a comforter of sorts he’ll usually surrender his when someone is in need. And yes, once every year or so you might find him at a nudist beach enjoying pure sun on all of his skin, and because he often isn’t the world’s fittest man there may be plenty of that.
Darren: Darren is a brickie’s labourer, which is handy in a booming property market, although women are no good to him unless he can root ‘em.
Darrin: Nope, he’s no brickie’s labourer. Darrin is artistic, sensitive and modern, and as such the scope of lifestyles available to him is as wide as his imagination. A little tip? He secretly loves the reactions of people who learn the correct spelling.
Darron: Not from the country, Darron wears scarfs on mild days, he has a large collection of designer socks and his dry cleaning bill is substantial.
Darryl: Completely unrelated to his rather plain step-brother below, Darryl is the debonair devil in sheep’s clothing.
Darryn: What an interesting chap. No, he doesn't lay bricks or build walls or dig as many holes as his cousin, Darren, although he does have a hard, shiny flat chunk at the top of him, or through the centre of him, somehow. Perhaps he's a top quality axe? He looks good though, and operates in his life within this nice sort of composition, do you know what I mean? And he listens, rarely talking over people.
Darshan: Darhsan appreciates a freshly ironed shirt and shiny shoes more than most. As something of a classist he will tell you that your presentation is vital if you’re going to succeed. And he won’t care if you or anyone deems this idea to be boring or not.
DArtagnan:
That's it. I'm changing my name to "Beep pop a-loo op, she's my baby".
(Just kidding.) Alexander Dumas lying in his grave would love this guy, I’m sure. Here in the modern world, D’Artagnan has pulled off a miraculous recovery. Far from ending up in rehab – although he has come close on occasion – he is the toast of his social set. I’ve no idea how he did it. And yes, he's in marketing.
Daryl: Nutritious and uncomplicated like a decent-sized potato.
Daryn: Behind the scenes is where Daryn excels. He's the gifted producer/editor who makes the show happen, and whom no one knows exists, which is just how he likes it. His ego never drives his life and he is good at what he does. Note also that 11% of Daryns have built some kind of sexual play space in their house.
Dashel: No, he's not a Dashhound, although he does have these long, ridiculous things hanging from his ears. Dashel, what's going on here, lad? You're dressed like a bloody slob, man. True, you're an 'artist' and so we expect a certain type of aesthetic I suppose, but seriously, you look like an unmade bed.
Dashiel: A smart and fast thinking young man who likes the idea of navigating. Rally car, aircraft and even blue water sailing - all of these things have crossed his mind as perhaps a job to aim for. Although sailing not so much, I suppose, because as often happens with those who think too much, he gets sea sick in the bath.
Dat: Is Dat a reiki healer? He should be if he isn’t. Pure of heart and radiantly optimistic, Dat conveys peace and understanding and everyone feels calm whenever they are near him.
Dathon: His parents are obsessed with Star Trek. The result is that Dathon loves to travel and is intrigued by new people and adventures. In all honesty, he is delighted every time he leaves the house.
Daud: He says he’s a muslim but we think he’s full of shit. A deeply convoluted man, Daud arrives at some new hair-brain scheme every 40 minutes or so, and he gets so engrossed in such ideas that he’d barely make it out of a burning building due to another philosophical discussion he couldn’t bear to finish prematurely.
Dav: Dav gets straight to it with a no-nonsense attitude that he somehow melds with a knack for keeping it real and light-hearted.
Dave: Dave is a light-weight dead-end, which is why everyone feels like they know him and why people feel immediately comfortable around him. If he isn’t saved by some other nickname then he needs to be barked at by a drill sergeant; “Stand up straight boy! Don’t slouch! Get some ambition in your life!”…..that kind of thing. In life therefore Dave is often so chilled out he's basically asleep.
Davey:
Death or glory is a wonderful, romantic ideal unless you’re on the losing side, eh lad? Are you lazy, stupid or are you an exhibitionist? We’ve got to hand it to you though, you’re a wonderful entertainer who is great for ratings. We have to ask, have you always been destined to wave away future responsibility for the sake of maximum fun in this moment? Should we envy or pity you? Having said all that, someone has to roll the dice - to show the rest of us what is possible if we throw caution to the wind.   
If you pull it off you’ll succeed spectacularly and if you don’t you’ll crash, catch on fire and die. It’ll make for great television either way, but you must know, Davey, the only reason so many of us are watching is just to see if you make it. Good luck!…
David: David is more serious than he appears because the heavy D’s at both ends weigh his name down like the legs of a North Sea oil platform, and to this end he may be too deep and sensitive for his own good. However, the ‘V’ in the middle provides a powerful launch pad for virtually anything. We wish him well.
Davin: Intelligent, slightly reserved and rarely a selfish lout. Like many good men Davin has never been in a fight in his life.
Davo: A big ball of coloured play-dough used by children under the age of 5.
Davy:
Davy, we don’t think you’ll mind, but you and your equally irresponsible twin brother are one and the same. So, head on over to Davey and we’ll see you on the other side, one way or another…
Love Management.
Dax: Good mates with Jordi, Max and Dane, Dax is a progressive man who, no matter how they come to know him, always surprises his friends with some of the little side projects he gets involved with. You know the Go Pro cameras all the surfers are sticking on their boards, these days? Dax thought of that years ago, even though he doesn't personally surf, and he loves his punk.
Daygen: A rather centred individual who takes a peculiar route in life. Not a dangerous or outlandish one, he's not that impulsive, for he'll assess the risk of his decisions before making the jump.
Dayrian: Deeper than your average river, Dayrian can remain within his walls for days on end. Hopefully he's planning and plotting for the next venture outside, which we hope is soon (and not sitting around staring at bloody video games for weeks). Mate, your nous is wasted staring at any kind of screen - Management.
Dayton: No, he's  not a critical thinker but he’s not dill either. In order to be great all he probably needs is to have serious decisions thrust upon him. Until this happens it’ll all be too flimsy and easy…
Daz: The friendly and generous bloke who, rather than medidate, likes working on his boat. He might even be a boat builder, who knows?
Dazza: Dazza does his best work at the Bachelor and Spinsters’ ball in the hours between 2am and 6am, such that people have no choice but to take notice of him.
Deacon: Peculiar and patient, yet determined at the same time, Deacon is like a beacon of hope and encouragement for those who know him and for many who don't. And he does all of this with barely an ego to be seen.
Deakin: Deakin writes a business plan and sticks to it. He also irons his socks.
Dean: Dean works at an abattoir where he operates a machine that kills cows by the hundreds. He eats lots of steak.
Deano: The free-thinking shit-stirrer. When life is good he’s there, front and centre. When it’s bad, you won’t see him for dust because he’ll be off somewhere else, trying to make it better.
Declan: Heralding from the same blood line as Sasha, Declan enjoys the luxury of being indulged by others, and he subsequently nearly always gets what he wants because people expect him to be himself.
Deegan: The Lurker. A nice fellow, but yes, a whole chunk of Deegan is completely latent.
Deion: Deion, the crew up here in the commentary box suggest you steer well clear of any girls called Shazza. On the flip-side, he earns an above average wage, which is nice, has a large group of modern friends, none of whom have ever held a rifle, and if push came to shove we like to think Deion could chop wood and make a fire if he had to. But we're not sure...
Demonthones: Demonthones, will you get off the stage and go back to work please? Your lunch break is over and if you want to act as a career then get yourself off to acting school or get an agent. Amen.
Dempsey: Dempsey is a bit of a goofball. You wouldn't say he's clumsy, exactly, and you wouldn't say he's awkward either, but he does have a very unique way of doing things. On the surface he seems a little bit shy, but like an engineer who can't switch off a heavily analytical mind, Dempsey processes things his way and in his time. It's usually worth the wait because while others rush head-long into some kind of stop-gap solution, Dempsey will disregard any negative (or frustrated) reactions near him as he considers the best option. The girl (partner) who gets Dempsey will be a cracker, for her (their) sense of humour will be extremely multi-layered and complex, as well.
Dempster: Charismatic and unusual, Dempster is a dark horse in nearly every category.
Den: Den deals with change brilliantly. Even something as banal as his wife/partner changing the furniture around is enough to get him frisky.
Denby: Having no idea what to do with his life, Denby attempted to fulfil a childhood fantasy by becoming a fireman. He ever told anyone of course, but he didn't do it to save people. What he really wanted was to be in a calendar of half-naked fireman. That way the girls would REALLY love him! (Happily, Denby became a great fireman, saved many many people and yes, you can see him in that calendar. He's that irreverent looking Mr. July smiling down at the cocker spaniel at his feet.)
Denis: Denis refuses to purchase new trousers unless the length is exactly correct. As a young man this penchant drove him loopy because of his height - he grew quite quickly, you see.
Dennis: Not exactly a rogue elephant, Dennis is more like a rogue daffodil, with the occasional exception of Dennis the Alcoholic.
Denver: More American hyperbole! Denver does okay, but again, the conversations his name produces are enough for him to shy away from the spotlight. So, he won’t be a CEO of anything big, and that’s a fine outcome anyway.
Denzel: Is he white? No? Excellent. Denzel has far more style and grace when he’s black. He’s into people, he’s educated and proactive, and he’s probably quieter in public than we would like. Well, unless he slipped into the bad habits of his twin brother, Denzil, but let’s not go there.
Denzil:
“Hey, wattup?" he says to his parents, having just arrived unannounced at the family home for the first time in nearly four years.
His father lifts his head up from the paper, looks him up and down and says, “Nope. You haven’t paid us off for the last money we gave you. Get a job!”
Derek: Faced with a room in which pandemonium reigns – people yelling and swearing, sobbing in some quarters, plates breaking, music blaring, tempers flared and emotions high – he will wander over to the cupboard, open the door peacefully, wait for silence to settle and ask, “Would anyone else like some cashews?”
Derick: Taxi driver. And no, he NEVER angles the rearview mirror in the hope of perving up girls' skirts, do you mate?
Dermott: The name of the physiological process whereby something is rolled into a sphere by peristaltic movements and the associated secretions of mucous. A fur ball spat out by any cat is a classic example. (Unless he’s the Irish Dermott, in which case he’s a semi-talented stand-up comedian.)
Derrick:
Ever see the movie Aliens - the second one? You know the one - where the cyborg-man plays stab-the-table-around-the-blokes-fingers-with-an-open-palm?

Anyway, the cyborg is genuinely funny, he's smart as hell and utterly subtle. Best of all he's curious and he wants to help. That, friends and neighbours, is Derrick to a tee.
Derry: Ah, the simple life. Do you remember what that's like Derry? That's all he wants, you understand. He doesn't want an ipad or blue tooth or wi-fi or a plasma or a hybrid or a chest wax. Derry, what happened brother? If you want to be a milkman then my advice is the following – toss out all that crap you don't need, get yourself a healthy donkey and cart, and get delivering. You'll get fit, you'll make enough to get by and you'll have friends, even if one of them is a healthy donkey. Amen.
Derryn: Not easily forgotten, Derryn approaches life like a displeased female hippo' who is unhappy about the proximity of the nearest tourist tinny. And she can be stealthy and tremendously powerful all at once. No, Derryn is not a she, but he wouldn't mind the inference because at the very least he is a well-travelled and open-minded man.
Derwent:
“Just quieten down there now please, Derwent. The rest of the class is trying to concentrate,” the teacher says to him.
Derwent obeys, and puts his joke away. He’s not an overtly rude student. Anyway, he’ll tell it later. In truth the teacher knows she has to reprimand him, but because he’s the funniest person in class she’s secretly disappointed that she can’t listen-in on the joke as well.
Des: Des is the name of a dust-covered Rolls Royce motorcar that’s been sitting in an uncle’s garage for nearly 20 years. No one is certain, of course, but there is a popular perception that if he was ever to wake from his slumber he would be a marvellous and reliable individual.
Despot: The world’s most gifted car mechanic. He’s damn-near telepathic, he admits to having performed more than 200 burnouts in his life and he speaks and deals with only the truth. “Hey,” he says, on the morning of the 25th of December, hungover from the night before, and ready to go again. “Merry Christmas....fucking!”
Dev: Dev is a cracker. As a busy optimist with a big smile he’s anything but lazy. He’s a great dancer, sports a large group of friends, arrives into romance easily and he treats his ladies and lovers well. Colourful shirts are his trademark.
Devin: Devin seems to cram a lot into a small space. Always thinking, he dislikes waste, be it something in a moment or on his plate, he's never late and he does what he says he's going to do.
Dex: Rarely lacking self-confidence and ambition, Dex is one of those people who, once they realise what it is they want to achieve, sets out a strategic plan which is not only well-thought out and logical, but is usually good for those around him. He never blows his own horn for the sake of attention and he doesn’t appreciate those who do. Having said all that, he’s not as serious as all this sounds, either. Indeed, to many, Dex is something of an enigma and all we can suggest is that you take some time and go discover Dex’s depths properly.
Dexter: The Swindler, The Joker, The Partier, etc etc.
Diallo: No, not diablo, he's not the devil, it's Diallo; like yellow after you wake up half asleep and forgetful. Is he a little dreamy in his approach? Well, probably yes, but only because a secret little part of his name, right before the l's, tries to disarm you by putting you to sleep. Nothing is taken too seriously in this court ladies and gentlemen, and because he's not stupid he tends to arrive where he aims. Not bad, really. But don't ask us what he does for a living, although he'd benefit from doing something near or in the ocean. Good luck.
Dick: The informal name hides the formal nature of the fellow. Mr. Cool, Mr. Deceptively Competitive and Mr. Genuine Nice Guy, he is. And he has a sense of humour. (It’s the only obvious part about him.)
Dicka: A normal fellow (he isn’t) who is in possession of a rapier wit. There were rumours that he once wore loud shirts and sported a short mans’ syndrome, but this theory has been subsequently debunked.
Didier: Exotic and eccentric, Didier rarely follows a well-trodden path. Friendly and honest, he always sees beyond the facade and his jokes and insights, therefore, are beyond many. Thank Christ.
Diego: Diego, you ain’t no hound dog, so stand up and be counted, boy!
Diesel: Detached and inert when he needs to be, and sometimes when even when he doesn’t, Diesel is one of the most determined individuals in the entire Kingdom.
Diet: Diet is dogmatic to the point of irritation. But, we, as a society of apathetic, lazy humans need him in case we ever decide to get off our arses and help. So, keep at it Diet and don't listen to the complaints. Management.
Dietmar: Mmm, you might imagine Dietmar to be a strict task master and someone without a sense of humour. After all, not many German-sounding names lend themselves to visions of high comedy, but Dietmar is something of an exception. Sure, he's a bit serious around the dinner table - I mean, you can't just pick up a bone in your hands and eat it - but mostly he looks for silly situations and odd people to amuse him. He's a bit silly himself, you see. Dietmar.
Digby: Digby has huge ears like Babaar the elephant. They turn red when he gets excited and if he’s really excited they start flapping.
Dimce: A pesky little bastard with a lightning sense of humour who can multi-task better than most men. He’s always on the look-out.
Dimitri: Dimitri’s first reaction to people he doesn’t know is one of utter warmth.
Dinesh: Is he Indian or Arabic, or maybe Persian? No one is quite sure, but my goodness, just have a look at him will you? He’s smooth. He’s patient. And he carries a certain kind of humorous grace that soothes. Nice work Dinesh.
Ding:
“Racing now and they burst from the blocks, drinking, drinking, drinking. Four rounds in and it’s Ding leading Ryan by a short half head. Touch and go as they make the final push for home. Empty glasses, tears and spittle cover the table and it’s a sad and sorry sight. LOOK OUT! A BRAWL HAS ERUPTED! YES, IT’S DING IN THE MIDDLE OF IT! He’s bleeding but he doesn’t seem to care and, yes, Ding prevails by half a length! Oooh, geeez, his head is going to hurt tomorrow, Brian, don’t you think?”
“Oh my word, yes, George. Well called. Tomorrow is not going to be a fun day for these boys.”
Indeed.
Ding, mate, get yourself an off switch. It might save your life one day.
Dinga: First to arrive at the party and last to leave, Dinga sobs when his sporting team loses and he loves his tats. His version of foreplay involves him asking the question, “Honey, feel like a tickle?”
Dingo:
Option A: Another Kiwi (what are they doing here?). His idea of the perfect meal is a special kind of slop that involves making a soup of mash potato containing at least one can of carnation milk, into which are dropped two or three lamb chops that have been incinerated to within an inch of their lives. Like his personality as a whole, the entire thing is borderline-carcinogenic.

Option B: Australian. Quick on his feet and he never looks back for too long. Dingo is certainly present. He’s silly but not stupid, kinky but not arrestable, and he’s a better lateral thinker than a skilled CIA operative, and certainly funnier.
Dino: Man, he's slippery. He's vanished from so many girls' morning bedrooms it isn't funny. Smart, with an excellent memory, Dino did eventually grow up. Yes, he can commit now, but he'll always be young at heart.
Dirk: Dirk is the only man in the animal kingdom who has willingly super-glued both of his hands to his own cock.
Dirty: Yes, Dirty is a cheeky bastard who, in his younger days, involved himself in all manner of dare-devil escapades. From the outside the risks he took were substantial, but Dirty is no fool - not now not then - and so they were always calculated and he was never in genuine peril…..we’re pretty sure. These days he’s actually quite responsible. Crazy eh?
Doc: Doc is super smart and possesses a photographic memory but he has very little common sense.
Dom: A rolling stone gathers no moss and Dom is at least that, then some. Friends and laughter fill his life and romance is never really an issue for such a positive soul. An intelligent cat who travels and experiments, Dom will be searching for the good times and the good people so long as he is able. Work-wise, he’ll lead bands, companies and work crews, always with a smile, and he can be a kinky fucker as well. Splendid work Dom.
Domenico:
Domenico - is he pig-headed?
Yep.
Is he funny?
Yep.
Is he broke?
Not usually.
Will he see a project through to the end?
If it’s worthy, yes.
Dominic: Dominic is passionate to the point of being lethal. He’s the sort of man, who, if he took to the back of a horse for the first time whilst in love and enraptured with the moment in general, may very well ride the animal to its death.
Don: A council worker’s shovel. He holds a lot of dirt and doesn’t mind grovelling in mud one iota. In fact he enjoys it.
Donald:
(Can we disregard that American President? He simply doesn't count as a fully compassionate, intelligent and friendly human.) Anyway, outside any kind of political jurisdiction Donald is like a donkey. Presuming he isn't either completely brainwashed or incredibly narrow-minded, he walks slowly, whether he’s carrying much weight or not, and he doesn’t understand why something like the pyramids generates all the fuss that they do. Donald is simple man and the good Donalds are humble farmers. These fellows are doing the best they can with the tools they possess, and they're considerate.

All that make sense?...
Donni: As a sufferer of the middle-child syndrome Donni has a temper and he can be selfish. But, Donni, forget all that for a minute. You do know that if you keep this mini-crime thing going it's only a matter of time before you get arrested or beaten up?
Donny:
Option A: Donny is in jail and he’s one of those prisoners who is liked by everyone, inmates and guards alike. 

Option B: Donny is that old bloke at the football club, without whom the place would fall apart. Who would go out and collect the footballs left alone on the ground after training is over? Who would turn off all the lights and lock up the sheds? Who would make sure there were enough oranges for the team on game day? And he knows the name of every player. 
And he asks for very little. (Maybe remember that come Christmas time.)
Donovan: His wardrobe consists only of Polo Ralph Lauren shirts with the gay polo player on the front. He aspires to be a sports reader on the TV news.
Dontay: Let's his friends make the decisions.
Doogan: Doogan lives in a house surrounded by rainforest. He spends most of his time in the nude, he eats his own vegetables and a myriad of birds and parrots call his house and garden home. Peace, love and contentment are Doogan's emotional companions and it's a wonderful thing. His car is held together with rust and humour.
Doogie: The man in control of the stash.
Doone: Doone is a fascinating creature. Over time he has evolved special receptors in his brain that have attuned his senses to the movements of rock within the earth’s crust, which is only one of his many eccentricities.
Doover: Doover snaps his fingers, even while doing something as banal as making a cup of tea.
Dorian: No one is as cluey as Oscar Wilde, Dorian, and neither are you. (Are you tired of the references?) Anyway, Dorian is intelligent, he is subdued sometimes although his ego, when it turns up, is hard to suppress or ignore. Keep an eye on that, eh chief? University educated, Dorian is never destined for the cues at the unemployment shop.
Doug: The name of the great moose head that’s hanging on the wall. He’s great to talk to when you come home, pissed as a mute.
Dougal: (No description needed.) Everybody....I’d like you to meet Dougal!
Douglas: "Here, give me that you bloody weakling," he barks, calling for the larger sledge hammer. Douglas.
Doyle: Doyle strictly adheres to the rules of engagement which exist inside and between families of means. Tradition is important here and Doyle, despite his easy nature, agrees wholeheartedly. Fucking boring if you ask me, then again I’m not lining myself up for a $12 million inheritance.
Dream: Originally from Nepal and originally named Nitten Redicum Bak Bak, Dream is the sort of fellow, who, when standing in the light of a roaring bonfire, rolling a cigarette and quietly swaying to music of the party, will elicit a sudden and instinctive scream of, “DREEEEEEEEEAAM!!”, from the two desperados sitting down, nearby, who have simultaneously spotted him, and who have given up any hope of finding anybody with a lighter. We’re lucky to have him.
Drew: Thoughtful. Quiet. Measured…at least, this is what people were led to believe. Perhaps he simply has no desire to be seen or heard by people he has no time for? Either way Drew is a meticulous planner and splendid fun.
Drex: Drex found God in a permaculture garden.
Dries: Dries walks tall and talks directly at you. Confrontation is a trifle for this fellow, although if he has any South African blood in him then it’s almost a given. He’s never going to be homeless, unless of course he gets tired of it all and decides to spend a few years living out there alone on the African Savanna eating the natives. Is he a wanker? Well, not with a rifle in his hand, no.
Dror: As soon as his (Israeli) government told him he had to join the army and, in all likelihood, try and shoot someone, that was it. He left the country, threw his passport out and wound up in either Byron Bay, Australia, or Varanasi, India, selling herbs at a specialist 'herb shop'. Funny as hell, Dror hasn't got an angry bone in his body.
Dru: Dru is far from a boring accountant. If he's partying, and he tends to do that very well, you can expect to see him in psychedelic clothing which looks the same whether you've ingested an acid tab or not. He tends to get bored at the drop of a hat so if you intend to marry Dru be mindful of that, although, as a reasonably savvy operator, chances are that he wouldn't select a partner who wasn't suited to him anyway. Know what I mean?
DS: The hidden artist. D.S is constructed of splendid moral fibre that enables him to exercise his substantial talents. From the ground up, he is designed perfectly for whatever it is that he decides to do with his life. And he is one funny individual.
Duane: Duane (and his twin brother Dwane) excel at church group, and yes, let's face it, somebody has to, and that's alright.
Dudley: A comic genius who doesn’t know it. He still can’t understand why the Queen gave him an Order of the Commonwealth but he forgot all that nonsense when he rushed-off to try and rescue the love of his life. Bravo Dudley! Bravo!!
Duds: Rarely blonde, Duds makes his way from space to space very smoothly, as if he’s a pool ball rolling across flat, green velvet. Women seem to be attracted to him easily although even he can’t really tell you how he ends up with these girlfriends. It just kind of happens. In terms of a career, he’s never doing what you’d think he’d be doing. He’s never that straight forward. That make sense?
Duke:
Some people just manage to land on their feet, no matter how much they’re in debt and no matter how many scars their ex-partners inflict upon them. 
Having said all that, Duke, some advice brother: If you find yourself with a wad of cash in your pocket, some day, don’t piss it up against a wall or bet the lot on a supposedly brilliant stock market tip. Take a few deep breaths and buy a chunk of property somewhere. No, it’s not the most daring thing to do and you’ll never make yourself famous for it, but once in a while you need to keep your feet planted on the ground....then again, maybe this is none of your business. Anyone got any ideas?...
Dummy: Alright, so he doesn’t have a clue how long it takes for photons of light to travel from the Sun to planet Earth, he has the table manners of a frothing pig and he’s never heard of Bolivia, let alone its capital city, but Dummy is a bona fide legend. Why? Because he is a lover and a fighter who susses people out in a flash – be they good, bad or useless – he always thinks laterally, he is a generous friend and when it comes to women he is a gracious gentlemen.
Duncan:
Option A:  The Solemn Priest. He is at home in front of his brethren. He is at home on the ocean. 

Option B:  The name of Sean’s cock.
Dundee: Dundee used to work at the crocodile park and he has almost certainly slept with Deidre.
Duran: Duran, if he’s called only that, never suffers from a dreadful dress sense. No way. His shoes are expensive and shiny and he’d rather look good than be broke.
Dusan: No, Dusan isn't an oaf although he does look kind of oafish. Perhaps it's just because he takes a while to answer. Not because he's daft or anything, he's actually very bright, but he likes to contemplate all possible results, that's all. Dusan.
Dustin: Polite and reliable, Dustin does a good job of cleaning up the edges.
Dusty: An unflappable character who rarely looks infuriated, probably because he rarely is. The days keep rolling on in life, and Dusty is very aware of the length and breadth of the whole process, which is why he keeps a steady hand.
Dutchy: Maybe he’s from Holland. Maybe he isn’t. It doesn’t matter. In the same vein as Clarky, Bill, Joe, Graeme, Jack, Jimmy and Bob, Dutchy is here for the stay, for the good times and the bad, he’ll laugh and help when he can, if he can, and in the wash-up all of us are glad that he is around. And when he’s gone we will mourn his absence. Cheers Dutchy.
Dwane: Dwane (and his twin brother Duane) excel at church group, and let's face it, someone has to.
Dwight:
“Yeah, I’m a great shot,” he’ll say, and the conviction and the intensity with which he says it have you believing him.
Truth is, he’s never picked up a rifle in his life, but sometimes we all need to stave off the inevitable. Dwight would make an excellent permanent political secretary.
Dylan: Like the rubber grip of a handle for anything that has a handle, Dylan looks okay and provides something for the universe, I suppose. He's quite proud of his hairdo. Indeed, he once crashed his car because he was staring at his reflection in the shop windows as he was driving along. Luckily he wasn't moving fast and the car in front only received minor dents.
